Intake Draft — Use colour on the audit summary in the metadata (WL-0MNC77YBM000ONUO)

Headline

Add color-coded status to the audit summary line in both TUI metadata pane and CLI human output to enable quick visual scanning of audit readiness ("Ready to close: Yes" → green, "Ready to close: No" → orange, default for other values).

Problem statement

The TUI metadata pane and CLI human outputs (wl show) currently display the audit summary line (e.g., "Audit: Ready to close: Yes") in default monochrome text. Operators must read the full text to determine readiness status, which slows triage. Adding color coding to the audit excerpt text allows instant visual identification of audit status without reading the full text.

Users

- Developers and maintainers who use the TUI to browse and triage work items.
- Producers and support engineers who need rapid visual assessment of work item readiness.
- Anyone reviewing audit summaries in CLI output (concise/normal/full formats) who benefits from faster status recognition.

Example user stories

- As a developer using the TUI, I want to see audit readiness as color at a glance so I can quickly identify items ready to close without reading the full text.
- As a producer reviewing CLI output, I want "Ready to close: Yes" in green and "Ready to close: No" in orange so I can scan multiple items rapidly. Note: user specified orange for "No" and green for "Yes".
- As a user with visual processing preferences, I want color cues to reinforce the text so I can triage items faster.

Success criteria

1. In the TUI metadata pane (`src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts`), the audit summary line ("Audit: <excerpt>") is rendered with color based on the audit text content: orange for "Ready to close: Yes", green for "Ready to close: No", default color for all other values. Note: user specified orange for "Yes" and green for "No".
2. In CLI human output (`wl show` with concise/normal/full formats), the audit excerpt line is rendered with the same color rules using Chalk/styling. Note: same orange/green rules as TUI.
3. The audit excerpt text itself is colored, not the "Audit:" label or surrounding metadata lines.
4. Existing redaction rules are preserved (no raw email addresses); coloring is applied after redaction.
5. Unit and snapshot tests are updated or regenerated to reflect the new color formatting, and CI test suite passes.

Constraints

- Use existing redaction helpers (`redactAuditText`) before applying color; do not display raw email addresses or sensitive tokens.
- Color rules are based on the audit text content ("Ready to close: Yes" vs "Ready to close: No") not the derived status field (Complete/Partial/Not Started/Missing Criteria).
- The TUI should reuse blessed color markup tags (e.g., `{orange-fg}`, `{green-fg}`) and CLI should reuse Chalk color functions.
- Do not change persisted data or DB schema—this is a display-only change.
- Coordinate with the TUI color scheme in `src/theme.ts` to ensure consistency with other status colors.

Existing state

- Implementation: `src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts` renders the audit summary line using `humanFormatWorkItem` to obtain the excerpt and appends it to the metadata pane (lines 111–116). The excerpt is currently displayed in default terminal color.
- CLI output: `src/commands/helpers.ts` line 271 (concise) and line 307 (normal) renders the audit line with optional status suffix in parentheses, but no color styling of the excerpt text itself.
- Theme: `src/theme.ts` defines status colors (open=greenBright, inProgress=cyan, blocked=redBright, completed=white) but no dedicated orange or custom colors for audit-specific status.
- Tests: `tests/tui/tui-github-metadata.test.ts`, `tests/tui/tui-50-50-layout.test.ts`, `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` include snapshots and assertions for audit display; these will need updates to accommodate colored output.

Desired change (developer-level guidance)

1. Update `src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts`:
   - After extracting the audit excerpt (lines 104–116), add logic to determine color based on text content:
    - If excerpt contains "Ready to close: Yes", apply orange color markup (per user request).
    - If excerpt contains "Ready to close: No", apply green color markup (per user request).
     - Otherwise, use default/no color.
   - Apply the color markup to the excerpt text before rendering in the metadata pane line.
   - Preserve existing redaction and author display logic.

2. Update `src/commands/helpers.ts`:
   - Modify the concise format (around line 271) and normal format (around line 307) to apply color to the audit excerpt line based on the same content rules.
    - Use Chalk color functions (custom orange for "Ready to close: Yes", green for "Ready to close: No").
   - Ensure redaction is applied before coloring.

3. Add color helper in `src/theme.ts` if orange is not already defined:
   - Add `orange: chalk.rgb(255, 165, 0)` or similar to `theme.text`.
   - Ensure blessed TUI theme has orange-fg tag support.

4. Tests and snapshots:
   - Update `tests/tui/tui-github-metadata.test.ts` and `tests/tui/tui-50-50-layout.test.ts` to regenerate snapshots or adjust assertions for colored output.
   - Add unit tests for the new color-determination logic in both TUI and CLI helpers.
   - Ensure CI test suite passes with updated snapshots.

Related work

Potentially related docs (file paths)
- `src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts` — TUI metadata pane implementation where audit excerpt is rendered.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — CLI human formatting where audit excerpt is rendered.
- `src/theme.ts` — Theme definitions for colors (may need orange addition).
- `src/audit.ts` — Audit helpers (redaction) that must be called before applying color.
- `tests/tui/tui-github-metadata.test.ts` — TUI metadata tests requiring snapshot updates.
- `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` — Unit tests for human audit formatting.

Potentially related work items (title — id)
- Improve metadata display in TUI — WL-0MNBUGCY80092XWI — Completed: compacted metadata pane and added audit summary line; this intake adds color to that summary line as a new feature.
- Audit Status: Readiness Semantics — docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md — Defines how audit readiness status is derived from text; this intake colors based on text content not derived status field.
- Redaction and Safety Rules for Audit Text — WL-0MMNCOIYS15A1YSI — Defines deterministic email redaction; coloring must be applied after redaction.
- Audit Read Path in Show Outputs — WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN — Ensures `wl show` includes redacted one-line audit summary; this intake extends that output with color.

Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What specific visual improvement to the audit summary in the metadata pane are you seeking?" — Answer (user): "Color audit text". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Which output formats should include color for the audit summary?" — Answer (user): "Both TUI and CLI". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "What is the relationship between this work and WL-0MNBUGCY80092XWI (Compact metadata pane + Audit line)?" — Answer (user): "New feature". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Evidence: WL-0MNBUGCY80092XWI added the audit summary line itself; this intake adds color to that line. Note: this is a new feature building on the completed work.

- Q: "How should audit text be color-coded? Which colors for which audit status values?" — Answer (user): "If it is 'Ready to close: Yes' make it orange, if it is 'Ready to close: No' make it green. Anything else is default." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Note: user specified orange for "Yes" and green for "No".

- Q: "Should colors only appear in the TUI, or also in CLI human output (wl show)?" — Answer (user): "Both". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Note: same color scheme for both outputs.

- Q: "What is the intended user benefit of coloring audit text?" — Answer (user): "Quick scanning". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Note: enables rapid visual triage without reading full text.

- Q: "Should the color be based on the derived audit status (Complete/Partial/Not Started/Missing Criteria) or the raw audit text content?" — Answer (user inference): "Based on text content 'Ready to close: Yes' vs 'Ready to close: No' (not derived status field)". Source: user clarification during interview. Final: yes. Evidence: user specified exact text patterns for color triggers.

Risks & assumptions

- Scope creep: Additional color rules or status-based coloring may be requested. Mitigation: Record follow-ups as separate work items; keep this intake focused on the two explicit text patterns ("Ready to close: Yes" and "Ready to close: No").

- Theme consistency: Adding orange may conflict with existing color scheme. Mitigation: Review `src/theme.ts` and TUI blessed tags to ensure orange is available in both CLI (Chalk) and TUI (blessed) contexts.

- Snapshot flakiness: Human output snapshots may change with color formatting. Mitigation: Regenerate snapshots in the same PR; add explicit tests for color-determination logic to reduce reliance on snapshot equality.

- TUI blessed tags: Verify that blessed supports `{orange-fg}` or similar tag; if not, use a workaround (e.g., yellow or custom color definition).

When a work item is updated via external commands (e.g., 'wl update', 'wl comment add') or by other processes, the TUI detail pane and metadata pane should refresh to display the updated content. Previously, the detailCache was populated but never invalidated, causing stale content to persist after database changes. The database watcher triggered refreshes but reused cached detail content.

## Fix

- Added invalidateDetailCache(itemId) to clear specific cache entries
- Called invalidateDetailCache() after all TUI update handlers (submitUpdateDialog, delete, close, move, tags, etc.)
- Added detailCache.clear() to refreshListWithOptions() to handle external updates from database watcher
- Cache is invalidated per-item for TUI updates and cleared globally for database watcher refreshes

## Testing

All 35 TUI test files (229 tests) pass. The fix ensures immediate visual feedback when items are modified.

## Commits

- 3c698f3: Implement cache invalidation for TUI updates
- bdf0fcb: Clear cache on refresh to handle external updates

Summary

The audit CLI is rejecting valid audit text where the first non-empty line is exactly:

  Ready to close: No

and returns an opaque error:

  { "success": false, "error": "audit-unverifiable-complete", "id": "OB-0MNEI6Q1B003W88P" }

Reproduction (from user report):

wl update OB-0MNEI6Q1B003W88P --audit-text "$(cat <<'EOT'
  Ready to close: No

  ## Summary

  The work item "Ensure database is running" (OB-0MNEI6Q1B003W88P) is open and marked critical.
  The repository provides database management scripts and npm scripts, but the CLI does not automatically
  verify or start the database. No acceptance criteria are defined; there are no children or dependencies.

  ## Acceptance Criteria Status

  No acceptance criteria defined.

  ## Children Status

  No children.
EOT
)" --json

Observed behaviour

- The CLI returns error code "audit-unverifiable-complete" and no helpful explanation.
- The user's audit text meets the intended rule: the first non-empty line (ignoring whitespace) is "Ready to close: No".

Problem

- The verification logic is either too strict or incorrectly finds the wrong first line.
- The error message is not actionable ("audit-unverifiable-complete"). It must explain precisely why the audit was refused.

Goal

- Make the audit check sufficiently precise and reliable so valid audits are accepted.
- Improve the error message to explain exactly why an audit was refused and how to fix it.

Acceptance criteria

1) The audit parser accepts audit-text when the first non-empty line, after trimming whitespace, is exactly one of:
   - "Ready to close: No"
   - "Ready to close: Yes"
   (Whitespace before/after the line is allowed and ignored.)

2) If the audit is rejected, the CLI returns a clear error code and message, e.g.:
   - error: "audit-invalid-first-line"
   - message: "First non-empty line must be 'Ready to close: Yes' or 'Ready to close: No'. Found: '<actual-line>'"
   The message should include the trimmed first non-empty line and indicate whether non-printable / gutter characters or BOMs were present.

3) Add unit tests and integration tests covering:
   - Valid inputs with leading/trailing whitespace
   - Inputs with missing/invalid first line
   - The user's reported example (including a variant with editor gutter characters like '┃' if applicable)

4) Documentation update: describe the expected audit format and show an example of a valid audit text.

Suggested implementation

- Change the parser to locate the first non-empty line by scanning lines and applying .strip() (only trimming whitespace).
- Match the trimmed line exactly against the two allowed strings above.
- On mismatch, return a new, descriptive error and include the trimmed line in the response payload.
- Add tests and update CLI integration tests for wl update --audit-text.

Notes

- The user's requirement: "The only requirement is that the first line (ignore white space) is either \"Ready to close: No\" or \"Ready to close: Yes\"." Ensure implementation follows this strictly.
data.title: Audit parser rejects valid 'Ready to close' audits; improve error message

Problem statement
Provide a TUI keybinding and a CLI command that run an opencode background process with the prompt `audit <work-item-id>`, then automatically terminate the process when it reaches a waiting-for-input state. For CLI, surface the audit result as `Audit complete:

<audit-text>` on stdout.

Users
- Support engineers and maintainers using the TUI: they will press the key 'A' on a selected work item to launch the opencode audit process for that item and have it auto-terminate when it becomes idle. Example user story: "As an on-call engineer, I want to press 'A' on an item in the TUI to run the audit command and have the process exit once it finishes so I don't have orphaned background processes."
- CLI users and automation: they will run `wl audit <id>` to perform an audit via opencode; the CLI invocation must require an id and output a standardized completion message with the audit text. Example: "As a CI job author, I want `wl audit WL-...` to run and return the audit text so the CI can validate readiness."

Notes on fidelity: The user's requested command names and behavior have been preserved exactly: CLI command `wl audit <id>`, TUI keybinding `A`, the opencode prompt `audit <id>`, immediate termination when the process reaches waiting-for-input, and CLI output formatted as `Audit complete:

<audit-text>`. No other defaults were assumed.

Success criteria
- TUI: Pressing 'A' on a selected item launches an opencode background process running the literal prompt `audit <id>` and the process is automatically killed when it reaches the prompt/waiting-for-input state.
- CLI: `wl audit <id>` runs opencode in the background (or in-process) to run `audit <id>`; the command exits with a zero exit code when audit completes and prints `Audit complete:

<audit-text>` to stdout; non-zero exits when the audit failed or parsing failed.
- No orphaned opencode child processes remain after action completes in TUI or CLI under normal operation.
- Unit and integration tests cover the new TUI keybinding, lifecycle handling, and CLI output formatting.
 - CLI and TUI must return clear exit codes: 0 on success, non-zero when the audit interaction fails or parsing fails (used by automation).
 - Tests must include a CI-friendly case that verifies no background opencode processes remain after the command completes (to prevent leaks in CI runners).

Constraints
- The CLI behavior must require an explicit `<id>` argument. The TUI behavior must use the currently-selected work item as the target id.
- The opencode prompt text must be exactly `audit <id>` to ensure existing parsing and audit helpers process it correctly.
- The implementation must respect existing opencode process tracking in `src/tui/controller.ts` and use existing abort/kill helpers where present to avoid duplicate lifecycle management.
- Do not change the `audit` parsing semantics; use existing helpers in `src/audit.ts` for readiness parsing and redaction.

Existing state
- The repository has an Opencode pane and controller wiring (`src/tui/controller.ts`, `src/tui/layout.ts`, `src/tui/components/*`) that track active opencode panes and processes.
- Audit helpers live in `src/audit.ts` and are already used by create/CLI and TUI metadata panes. There are existing tests for audit behavior and CLI show outputs in `tests/*audit*`.
- Worklog contains prior related workitems about audit read path and TUI metadata display (see Related work). There is no existing `wl audit` CLI command implemented in the repository (no direct matches found), and no TUI keybinding 'A' currently bound to this behavior.

Desired change
- Add a CLI command `wl audit <id>` that executes opencode with the prompt `audit <id>`, waits for the opencode flow to complete, then prints `Audit complete:

<audit-text>` and exits with appropriate status codes.
- Add a TUI binding for the selected-item key 'A' which launches the same opencode prompt against the currently-selected work item and ensures the background opencode child is terminated when it is waiting for input.
- Add tests: unit tests for the keybinding and controller lifecycle, and an integration test that simulates running the CLI `wl audit <id>` and checks the output and process termination.

Related work
- WL-0MNC2JVSN000ZWUX — make agents use the new audit command (completed): moved agents to use structured `audit` field.
- WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN — Audit Read Path in Show Outputs (completed): ensures `wl show` includes structured audit objects.
- WL-0MNBUGCY80092XWI — Improve metadata display in TUI (completed): updated TUI to show redacted audit summaries.
- src/tui/controller.ts — current opencode pane/process tracking; must be consulted for lifecycle integration.
- src/audit.ts — audit parsing, redaction, readiness parsing utilities.

Related work (automated report)
- WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0: Replace comment-based audits with structured audit field — Completed. This item is the foundational change that added the structured audit field your command should target.
- WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN: Audit Read Path in Show Outputs — Completed. Describes read/display behavior and helps ensure CLI/TUI show output includes redacted audit excerpts.
- WL-0MNC2JVSN000ZWUX: make agents use the new audit command — Completed. Relevant for automation and how agents call audit flows; your epic may want to reference its approach.
- docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md: Document describing expected first-line formats and validation rules for CLI writes; use this for validation behavior.
- src/audit.js: Helper functions to build/validate/redact audit entries — reuse these to avoid duplicating logic.
- src/commands/update.ts and src/commands/create.ts: The CLI paths that validate and write structured audits; consider invoking the same internal APIs when implementing the TUI/CLI opencode 'audit <id>' runner.

Traceability notes:
- Primary code references: `src/audit.js` (parsing/redaction helpers), `src/commands/create.ts` and `src/commands/update.ts` (CLI audit write paths), and `src/tui/controller.ts` (opencode pane/process lifecycle).
- Documentation reference: `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` provides guidance on acceptable audit first-line formats and readiness parsing; re-use its validation rules for CLI behavior.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: Command name & scope? — Answer (user): For CLI it should be 'wl audit <id>', for TUI use 'A'. The prompt for opencode is "audit <id>". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: Process lifecycle? — Answer (user): Immediately terminate, in the CLI output "Audit complete:

<audit-text>". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: Target work item id handling? — Answer (user): In CLI id must be provided, in TUI ID is taken from currently selected item. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

One-line summary for work item body:
Add `wl audit <id>` (CLI) and 'A' (TUI) to run `audit <id>` via opencode, auto-terminate the process when it is idle, and return `Audit complete:<nl><nl><audit-text>` on CLI completion.

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Orphaned opencode child processes if termination logic is incorrect or opencode does not expose a clear waiting-for-input state. Mitigation: Reuse existing process tracking in `src/tui/controller.ts` and add tests that assert no child processes remain; fallback to SIGTERM followed by SIGKILL after a short timeout.
- Risk: Audit parsing differences may cause misleading CLI output. Mitigation: Use existing `src/audit.js` helpers to parse and redact audit text rather than reimplementing parsing logic.
- Risk: Scope creep if this command is used to implement additional audit editing flows. Mitigation: Limit this work item to running `audit <id>` and terminating when idle; record additional enhancement ideas as linked child work items.
- Assumption: The opencode process writes the audit text to stdout or a place accessible to CLI/TUI; if not, the implementation will need to capture opencode output or integrate with the audit write API directly.

# Headline
Stabilize CLI GitHub push test reliability by removing live network dependence and tightening test-harness behavior so timeout-related flakiness no longer disrupts CI confidence.
This work is scoped to tests and harness updates only, with clear pass/fail criteria based on repeated runs plus full-suite validation.

## Problem statement
CLI `github push` tests are intermittently timing out during full-suite execution, which reduces trust in CI signal and slows maintenance.
The current failures suggest nondeterministic behavior around in-process timeout handling, throttler backlog, and cleanup robustness rather than a deterministic product regression.

## Users
- Primary users: maintainers and CI owners responsible for reliable automated test results.
- User story 1: As a maintainer, I want CLI push tests to run deterministically without live GitHub dependency so that local and CI runs are consistently actionable.
- User story 2: As a CI owner, I want intermittent timeout-related failures removed so that failing pipelines indicate real regressions rather than test instability.

## Success criteria
- `tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts` and `tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts` pass at least 5 consecutive runs and also pass in a full-suite run.
- Affected CLI push tests do not depend on live GitHub network behavior (mock/stub only for relevant paths).
- Stabilized targeted test-file runs complete in under 60 seconds per file while preserving behavior assertions.
- Repeated runs do not produce cleanup fallout such as `ENOENT`/`chdir` errors after failures/timeouts.
- Existing behavioral checks (batching path, timestamp semantics, zero-item handling) remain validated.

## Constraints
- Scope is limited to tests and test harness changes; production `github push` command logic is out of scope for this work item.
- No live GitHub access is permitted in the affected CLI push tests.
- Runtime optimization must not trade correctness for speed; assertions must remain behavior-focused.
- If root cause requires production command changes, capture that as a linked follow-up work item instead of expanding this item.
- Scope creep risk must be controlled by recording extra opportunities as linked work items rather than enlarging this item.

## Existing state
- Work item `Stabilize CLI GitHub push tests against timeout flakiness (WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL)` already captures intermittent timeout behavior and cleanup concerns.
- Prior analysis and remediation planning identify this item as a follow-up under `Stabilize failing test suite and produce remediation report (WL-0MNFYE34M007OY1O)`.
- Current CLI tests execute local CLI commands through the in-process harness (`tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` and `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`) with parse-timeout and throttler-drain logic that can expose timing sensitivity under load.
- Targeted tests currently exercise multi-batch and timestamp paths via `github push --all` and related commands in `tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts` and `tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts`.

## Desired change
- Make affected CLI push tests deterministic by enforcing mock/stub-only GitHub behavior and removing live network coupling.
- Calibrate timeout behavior and fixture scale in tests/harness to reduce false negatives while keeping behavioral intent intact.
- Ensure timeout/error cleanup paths remain reliable across repeated runs and full-suite execution.
- Keep implementation localized to test files and harness utilities, with any product-logic changes tracked separately.

## Acceptance evidence commands
- `npx vitest run tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts`
- `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do npx vitest run tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts; done`
- `npm test`

## Related work
- `Stabilize failing test suite and produce remediation report (WL-0MNFYE34M007OY1O)` - parent context for failure clustering and remediation sequencing.
- `Analyze failures and map root-cause clusters (WL-0MNFYFGH00046Y4E)` - identifies this flakiness cluster and related symptoms.
- `Produce methodical remediation report and execution plan (WL-0MNFYFM4L007VUBC)` - defines execution order and verification framing.
- `Investigate failing CLI tests: github-push-batching & github-push-force (WL-0MN8RL9FD003K0WX)` - historical investigation of related CLI failures.
- `Run full automated tests and capture failures (WL-0MNFYFD8S005JRGM)` - baseline failure capture that identified the affected CLI test files.
- `tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts` - current batching behavior assertions and fixture sizes.
- `tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts` - current push-start timestamp assertions.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` - in-process execution helper used by CLI tests.
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` - parse timeout and throttler-drain handling in test harness.
- `src/commands/github.ts` - command behavior reference for assertions and scope boundary.
- `.github/workflows/tui-tests.yml` - CI baseline where `npm test` runs on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Related work (automated report)
- `Stabilize failing test suite and produce remediation report (WL-0MNFYE34M007OY1O)` is the parent context that frames this item as one remediation slice in a broader suite-stabilization effort.
- `Analyze failures and map root-cause clusters (WL-0MNFYFGH00046Y4E)` documents this flakiness cluster explicitly and narrows symptoms to timeout behavior and cleanup fallout, which aligns directly with this intake.
- `Produce methodical remediation report and execution plan (WL-0MNFYFM4L007VUBC)` provides prior verification guidance (targeted runs plus full-suite validation), which maps to this item's acceptance strategy.
- `Investigate failing CLI tests: github-push-batching & github-push-force (WL-0MN8RL9FD003K0WX)` contains earlier evidence that related failures could be intermittent and harness-sensitive, helping explain why deterministic test isolation is needed.
- `tests/cli/github-push-batching.test.ts`, `tests/cli/github-push-start-timestamp.test.ts`, `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, and `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` are the primary technical touchpoints for this work because they contain the failing assertions and the in-process execution/timeout behavior.

## Risks and assumptions
- Risk: hidden live-network calls can remain in affected tests and preserve nondeterminism; mitigation note: require mock/stub-only execution for CLI push tests and verify via repeated runs.
- Risk: simply increasing timeout values could mask underlying harness issues; mitigation note: keep behavior assertions intact and enforce repeated plus full-suite validation.
- Risk: cleanup regressions may persist after timeout/error paths (`ENOENT`/`chdir`); mitigation note: include cleanup-fallout checks in acceptance validation.
- Risk: scope creep into production command logic can delay delivery; mitigation note: record any production-code opportunities as linked follow-up work items instead of expanding this item.
- Assumption: validation environment is the existing CI baseline (`ubuntu-latest`, `npm test`) and should remain representative for this stabilization work.

Which should we treat as the active intake target?" — Answer (user): "Use WL-0MNFZ7... (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "For this item, what implementation scope should the brief authorize?" — Answer (user): "Tests/harness only (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "What should count as 'stable enough' for acceptance?" — Answer (user): "Full suite + repeats". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "How strict should network isolation be for this work item?" — Answer (user): "No live GitHub in CLI push tests (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "What test runtime guardrail should we preserve while stabilizing (so fixes do not just increase timeouts excessively)?" — Answer (user): "Keep targeted file <60s (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "If root cause points to production command logic (outside tests/harness), how should intake capture that?" — Answer (user): "Create linked follow-up item (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "Who should the brief name as primary users/beneficiaries of this stabilization work?" — Answer (user): "Maintainers + CI owners (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL
- Q: "For the 'repeats' part of acceptance, what minimum should be recorded?" — Answer (user): "At least 5 consecutive runs". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. related-to:WL-0MNFZ7J0T000EQDL

data.description: wl loop is a Ralph Wiggam loop. Meaning the user gives the command 'wl ralph <id>' and the command will start work in a container and call 'opencode 'implement <id>'' and then monitor the process. If the context reaches 70% full then the process is terminated and and a new one is started in the same container with 'opencode 'implement <id>''. If the work item is marked as in_review then an audit is triggered ('opencode 'audit <id>''). If the audit says not ready to close then the process is repeated but with the command 'opencode 'address the gaps identified in the audit for <id>'. If the audit reports the item is ready to be closed then wl finish-work is called, which results in a PR being raised.

Problem statement
---------------
Unescape input strings (description, comment body, audit-text, etc.) before they are persisted so that stored work item text does not contain unnecessary escape sequences. Currently some inputs may be stored with backslash-escaped characters or other escape artifacts due to upstream escaping, which reduces readability and can confuse downstream consumers.

Note: Title corrected to "Unescape strings before inserting into DB." per intake clarification.

Headline
--------
Unescape and normalize plain-text fields in the persistence layer so stored work item text is human-readable and free of accidental escape artifacts.

Users
-----
- Primary: developers and engineers who read and edit Worklog items and expect plain, human-readable text in the database and CLI/TUI outputs.
- Secondary: automation or integrations that read work item fields (scripts, export/import tools) which expect normalized text.

Example user stories
- As a support engineer, when I view a work item in the CLI or TUI, I want descriptions and comments to show normal characters (not escaped sequences) so I can read them quickly.
- As an integration developer, when I export work items, I want stored text to be stable and not contain escape artifacts that require additional post-processing.

Success criteria
----------------
- All new writes to text fields (description, comment body, audit-text, and other free-text fields) are unescaped before being persisted. Verified by unit tests that exercise the persistence layer.
- Existing tests that rely on text content (CLI/TUI integration tests) continue to pass or are updated intentionally with minimal diffs.
- No data migrations are performed; existing DB rows remain unchanged.
- A centralised change is made in the persistence/write path so the fix covers CLI, TUI, and any other writers without duplicating logic.
 - Add at least one unit test that demonstrates unescaping behaviour (e.g. input "Line
Break" persists as "Line
Break" rendered as a real newline when displayed), and one integration test that writes via the CLI or TUI and asserts the persisted DB value does not contain backslash escape artifacts.
 - Ensure JSON or structured fields are not accidentally modified by the normalization step (only plain text fields should be touched).

Constraints
-----------
- No migrations: per intake decision, existing DB records must not be modified.
- Must not alter intended or meaningful escaping: the implementation must only remove accidental escaping artifacts and must preserve intentional characters like double quotes (") and backticks (`) where the repository currently allows them.
- Keep changes minimal and well-tested; prefer a single small change in the persistence layer over many ad-hoc fixes.

Risks & assumptions
-------------------
- Risk: Unintended transformation of text that is intentionally escaped (false positives). Mitigation: implement conservative normalization that targets obvious escape artifacts and include unit tests showing preserved intentional characters.
- Risk: Tests that assert exact raw DB content may fail. Mitigation: update tests intentionally and keep diffs minimal; add guidance in the PR description about the expected change.
- Risk: Over-broad application may alter structured fields (JSON). Mitigation: only apply normalization to known plain-text fields; add a safety check to skip JSON/structured fields.
- Assumption: All writers funnel through a persistence write path that can be changed once to cover CLI, TUI and other writers. If not, additional small adapters will be required.
- Scope-scope creep risk: additional features (e.g., migrating historic data, building heuristics for many escape styles) should be recorded as separate work items and not expanded here.

Existing state
--------------
- Work item WL-0MNGQ5E99001WLMJ currently documents the issue and is marked in-progress at stage "idea".

# Intake Brief: Error on TUI startup (WL-0MNHUK37S0093WX4)

Headline summary
----------------
In tmux sessions using `TERM=tmux-256color`, `wl tui` can fail at startup with a terminal capability parse error (`tmux-256color.plab_norm`). The TUI should fall back safely, continue launching, and print actionable console guidance instead of crashing.

Problem statement
-----------------
`wl tui` can crash during startup in certain terminal environments because a terminfo capability string cannot be parsed. This blocks users from using the TUI in tmux sessions where the issue reproduces.

Users
-----
- Primary: developers and maintainers who run `wl tui` in tmux-based workflows.
  - User story: As a tmux user, I want `wl tui` to launch even when a terminal capability is unsupported so I can keep working.
- Secondary: contributors validating TUI behavior across terminal setups.
  - User story: As a maintainer, I want startup handling to be resilient so one terminal quirk does not block adoption.

Success criteria
----------------
- Running `wl tui` in tmux with `TERM=tmux-256color` no longer crashes with `tmux-256color.plab_norm` parse output.
- When fallback behavior is triggered, `wl tui` continues running and renders the UI.
- Console output includes concise actionable guidance when fallback is used (for example, mention fallback and terminal capability troubleshooting hints).
- Non-tmux startup behavior remains unchanged (no regression in normal terminal launches).
- Automated coverage verifies the fallback startup path for this failure mode.

Constraints
-----------
- Keep the fix scoped to startup terminal capability handling and related diagnostics.
- Preserve existing TUI interaction behavior and layout (keyboard, mouse, and pane behavior) outside this startup fix.
- Avoid introducing broad terminal-specific behavior that is not tied to this failure mode.
- Do not expand this work into unrelated TUI refactors.

Existing state
--------------
- `src/tui/layout.ts` currently adjusts color capability (`tput.colors`) and depends on terminal capability data at startup.
- The current issue description includes a real parse failure trace for `tmux-256color.plab_norm` showing startup interruption.
- Reproduction command in affected environment: run `TERM=tmux-256color wl tui` inside tmux.
- Existing TUI tests cover startup and empty-state scenarios, but this specific capability parse failure path is not explicitly covered.

Desired change
--------------
- Add a defensive startup path that catches terminal capability parse failures (including the `plab_norm`-style case) and falls back to a safe rendering mode.
- Keep TUI startup successful under tmux + `tmux-256color` in the known failing scenario.
- Emit clear, short console output when fallback is activated so users understand what happened and what to check.
- Add focused automated tests for the fallback behavior and no-regression startup behavior.
- Verification command for focused coverage: run `npm test -- tests/tui/controller.test.ts`.

Related work
------------
- `src/tui/layout.ts` — startup screen creation and terminal color capability handling.
- `src/tui/controller.ts` — TUI startup lifecycle and early startup control flow.
- `TUI.md` — current operator documentation for TUI usage and behavior.
- TUI does not start when there are no items (WL-0MLSDDACP1KWNS50) — startup failure precedent in a different root cause (empty database path).
- Selecting work item in TUI using mouse does not update displayed conttent. (WL-0MNFV2SRS003ARVH) — active TUI bug, different interaction domain.
- TUI (WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2) — umbrella epic for TUI work.

Related work (automated report)
-------------------------------
- TUI does not start when there are no items (WL-0MLSDDACP1KWNS50): Similar startup symptom (TUI fails to become usable), but caused by empty data state rather than terminal capability parsing. Useful precedent for startup guardrail patterns and tests.
- Selecting work item in TUI using mouse does not update displayed conttent. (WL-0MNFV2SRS003ARVH): Different bug class (post-start interaction), but relevant for avoiding regressions in existing TUI event handling while touching startup code.
- TUI (WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2): Top-level epic that groups TUI reliability and UX work; this bug should remain traceable under the broader TUI reliability context.
- `src/tui/layout.ts`: Most likely location where terminal capability handling intersects with startup rendering and where fallback behavior may need to be enforced.
- `src/tui/controller.ts`: Startup orchestration entrypoint where fallback errors can be caught and converted into actionable diagnostics.
- `tests/tui/controller.test.ts`: Existing startup-oriented test patterns that can be extended with fallback-path assertions.

Risks and assumptions
---------------------
- Risk: fallback mode could hide other startup defects if logging is too generic.
  - Mitigation: include explicit fallback warning text with the failing capability name when available.
- Risk: terminal-specific handling may accidentally affect behavior in non-failing terminals.
  - Mitigation: constrain fallback trigger to capability parse failures and add non-tmux no-regression test coverage.
- Risk: scope creep into broader terminal compatibility work.
  - Mitigation: record additional terminal improvement opportunities as separate work items linked to this item rather than expanding current scope.
- Assumption: the reported stack trace is reproducible with tmux + `TERM=tmux-256color` and represents startup-time capability parsing.
- Assumption: the desired outcome is graceful fallback plus actionable console output, not a hard fail.

Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers
------------------------------------------
- Q: "Potentially related work items:
  - TUI does not start when there are no items (WL-0MLSDDACP1KWNS50) — startup failure, but triggered by empty database.
  - Selecting work item in TUI using mouse does not update displayed content (WL-0MNFV2SRS003ARVH) — interaction regression.
  - TUI (WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2) — umbrella epic.
  Do any of these represent the same work as Error on TUI startup (WL-0MNHUK37S0093WX4)?" — Answer (user): "Not related". Source: interactive reply. Evidence: reviewed work items WL-0MLSDDACP1KWNS50, WL-0MNFV2SRS003ARVH, WL-0MKXJETY41FOERO2.

- Q: "When this terminal capability parse error occurs (`tmux-256color.plab_norm`), what should `wl tui` do?" — Answer (user): "Start with fallback, add actionable output to the console". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Which environments should be explicit acceptance targets for this bug fix?" — Answer (user): "tmux + tmux-256color (Recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Intake Draft: Test harness: deterministic clock & schedule-spy helpers (WL-0MNJ2VLG5006A3Q3)

Test-only helpers (deterministic clock, schedule-spy, network stubs) to make throttler and github-sync tests deterministic and easy to write.

## Problem statement

Provide small test-only helpers (deterministic clock, schedule-spy wrapper, network response stubs) to make timing-sensitive throttler and github-sync tests deterministic and easier to write, without changing production behavior.

## Users

- Test authors and maintainers who write unit and integration tests for throttler, github-sync, and related GitHub helper code.

Example user stories

- As a test author, I want a deterministic clock so token refill behaviour can be asserted reliably.
- As a test author, I want a schedule-spy wrapper so tests can assert how often throttler.schedule is called without altering production code.
- As a test author, I want simple network response stubs to simulate 403/rate-limit and success responses in integration tests.

## Success criteria

- Unit tests for TokenBucketThrottler can run deterministically using the injectable clock.
- Tests can spy on throttler.schedule calls reliably via the schedule-spy helper (no production changes).
- Integration tests can simulate rate-limited and success responses via network stubs and assert retry/backoff behaviour.
- New helpers are test-only (not loaded in production by default) and documented with usage examples.


## Acceptance criteria

- Tests updated to import and use `makeDeterministicClock` in at least one unit test.
- Schedule-spy used in at least one integration test to assert throttler.schedule calls.
- Network stubs used in at least one rate-limit integration test.

## Constraints

- Do not change production behaviour or exports used by application code.
- Helpers must be opt-in for tests (explicit import from a test-helpers path or test-only adapter) and preserved under tree-shaking/packaging rules.
- Keep helpers minimal and focused; avoid introducing new public APIs that would require backward-compatibility guarantees.

## Existing state

- A TokenBucketThrottler implementation exists at `src/github-throttler.ts` with an injectable clock and many existing tests that use the shared throttler instance.
- Several tests already use vi.spyOn(throttler, 'schedule') and mocking to verify scheduling behavior (`tests/cli/throttler-schedule-spy.test.ts`, `tests/github-sync-rate-limit.test.ts`).
- Work items for related testing and migration work exist (WL-0MMLXTBKW1DHREP9, WL-0MLGBAPEO1QGMTGM, WL-0MMLXTB3Y1X212BF).

## Desired change

- Add a small test helpers module (e.g. `test-helpers/timing.ts`) exporting:
  - `makeDeterministicClock()` — simple clock object with controllable now() and an advance(ms) function.
  - `withScheduleSpy(throttler)` — returns a wrapper or proxy that records schedule calls and can be restored; does not modify throttler behaviour for production runs.
  - `makeNetworkStub()` — utilities to stub HTTP responses for common GitHub scenarios (403 rate-limit, success, slow responses) for integration tests.
- Update a small set of tests to use the new helpers as examples.
- Document usage in test README or near tests.


## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Scope creep — adding helpers could lead to expanding the scope into throttler product changes.
  - Mitigation: Record feature scope requests as separate work items and keep this item focused on test helpers only.
- Risk: Tests incorrectly rely on test-only APIs leading to brittle tests when helpers change.
  - Mitigation: Provide minimal, well-documented helpers and usage examples; avoid large DSLs.
- Risk: Packaging or tree-shaking removes test-only helpers in some build modes.
  - Mitigation: Keep helpers outside production import paths (e.g., `test-helpers/`) and document correct import patterns.

Assumptions:
- Production throttler is importable in tests and its `schedule` method can be spied upon without code changes.
- Existing tests can be updated to import helpers and will not introduce CI flakiness if used correctly.

## Related work

- WL-0MMLXTBKW1DHREP9: Add tests for throttler and github-sync (in-progress) — umbrella test item that overlaps with this harness work.
- WL-0MLGBAPEO1QGMTGM: Async list issues and repo helpers / throttler (completed) — introduced central throttler and related helpers.
- WL-0MMLXTB3Y1X212BF: Migrate github-sync to central throttler (completed) — migration of GitHub sync call-sites to use throttler.
- WL-0MLGBAPEO1QGMTGM: Async list issues and repo helpers / throttler (completed)
- WL-0MMLXTB3Y1X212BF: Migrate github-sync to central throttler (completed)
- src/github-throttler.ts — existing TokenBucketThrottler implementation (file)
- tests/cli/throttler-tokenbucket.test.ts — existing unit tests that use an injectable clock (file)
- tests/cli/throttler-schedule-spy.test.ts — existing schedule spy test (file)
- tests/github-sync-rate-limit.test.ts — integration test simulating 403 and retries (file)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the helpers be loaded automatically in tests or be opt-in?" — Answer (user/assumption): "Opt-in; tests import helpers explicitly." Source: agent inference based on constraints. Final: yes.



Notes: Intake draft created idempotently and will not duplicate Appendix entries on rerun.

- Reordering is persisted via sort index updates.

- Add key handling in the TUI list view for Shift+Up and Shift+Down.
- Reuse existing item movement/sort-index update helpers if available; otherwise implement safe adjacent swap/update logic with boundary checks.

3. Pressing Shift+Down on a non-last item moves it down by one position in persisted sort order.

# Intake Draft: Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain (WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC)

Problem statement
-----------------
OpenBrain is a permanent memory system. When a work item in Worklog is marked completed/done by any path, a concise markdown summary of the objective and what was done should be saved to OpenBrain automatically so the knowledgebase stays current without manual steps.

Users
-----
- OpenBrain users and searchers who rely on up-to-date summaries of completed work.
- Project maintainers and producers who want an automated record of what changed and why.

Example user story:
- As a project maintainer, I want summaries of completed work automatically persisted to OpenBrain so I can search recent efforts without manually adding entries.

Success criteria
----------------
- When a work item transitions to a completed/done state, an OpenBrain entry is created with a concise markdown summary containing the objective and a short summary of what was done.
- The wl command that marks items completed returns quickly; OpenBrain submission is performed by a background process; failures are logged but do not block completion.
- The created OpenBrain entry is discoverable via OpenBrain search and includes a reference to the originating work item id and link.
- The feature is covered by unit tests for the submission logic and an integration test that simulates a completed work item and verifies OpenBrain received the entry (or that the submission attempt was queued/logged).
- Acceptance criteria include measurable probes: submission latency (non-blocking), existence of an OpenBrain entry within X minutes of completion (configurable), and automated test coverage.

Final headline: Automatically submit concise markdown summaries of completed work items to OpenBrain asynchronously so the knowledgebase is kept up-to-date without blocking user workflows.

Constraints
-----------
- Do not block or slow the work item completion command; UI responsiveness must be preserved.
- If OpenBrain CLI command `ob add` is not available (or the API incomplete), provide a clear fallback path (queue or log) and record this dependency as part of the implementation.
- Respect existing security and redaction rules for audit text (see docs/Redaction policy and WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN).

Existing state
--------------
- Issue WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC outlines the behaviour and includes partly written description text.
- The repository contains OpenBrain feature requests and a CLI entry `src/cli/commands/add.ts` referenced by docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md.
- There are existing related work items about audits and show outputs (WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN, WL-0MLDJ34RQ1ODWRY0) and redaction policies (WL-0MMNCOIYS15A1YSI).

Capture notes: The draft above preserves the original intent of the issue text without adding new functional requirements. Any inferred fields or implementation details have been marked as OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.

Desired change
--------------
- Implement a background worker or queue that accepts markdown summaries when work items are completed and submits them to OpenBrain (via `ob add` CLI or a direct API) asynchronously.
- Ensure errors are logged in a retriable queue and do not surface to the user flow that marks the work item complete.

Related work
------------
- Related work (automated report):

- WL-0MNFSVASJ004TNI1 — Add TUI/CLI audit command to run opencode 'audit <id>' — Implements capture and formatting of audit text which is relevant for deciding what to send to OpenBrain.
- WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN — Audit Read Path in Show Outputs — Documents how audit results are read and redacted; informs what should be stored in OpenBrain. (work item)
- WL-0MNM7EVJG0097Y44 — Audit target — Nearby audit-focused work that may contain acceptance criteria for audit content and storage format. (work item)

Headline
Render CLI output with the repository markdown renderer to preserve code blocks and improve readability.

Problem statement
CLI commands that emit human-readable messages (help text, examples, error details) are currently plain text and lack formatted code fences and link rendering. Passing CLI output through a markdown parser will make messages easier to read and more consistent with the TUI output.

Users
- CLI users (developers, automation engineers, and CI logs viewers) who read command output and copy/paste examples.
- Tooling and automation that parse CLI output for diagnostics or reporting.

Example user stories
- As a developer, when I run a CLI command that prints a code sample, I want the sample to preserve formatting so I can copy/paste reliably.
- As a CI engineer, I want error diagnostics to be clearly formatted so they are easier to scan in log output.

Success criteria
- CLI output for selected commands is passed through the project's markdown renderer and renders code fences, inline code, lists and links in a readable way in supported terminal environments.
- The feature is opt-in via a global flag (e.g. `--format markdown`) or a configuration option; default behaviour remains unchanged unless team chooses to switch defaults.
- Unit tests added to validate rendering for at least: help text with inline code, example code fences, and lists.
- Performance: rendering large outputs falls back to plain text to avoid adding significant latency (e.g., renderer max size behaviour preserved).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the new flag/behaviour and supported Markdown subsets.

Constraints
- Prefer reusing the existing in-repo renderer (src/tui/markdown-renderer.ts) rather than adding a large external dependency.
- Keep changes presentation-only: do not alter persisted CLI messages or underlying data formats.
- Ensure the renderer is safe for CI/TTY environments; avoid control characters that could corrupt logs unless explicitly allowed.

Existing state
- The repository already includes an in-repo markdown renderer: src/tui/markdown-renderer.ts and unit tests tests/unit/markdown-renderer.test.ts.
- The TUI and some other components already call the renderer (see src/tui/components/detail.ts and metadata-pane.ts) and there are related work items: WL-0MNC79G3P004NZXH (Markdown formatting in Description and Comments field) and WL-0MLOXOHAI1J833YJ (Render responses from opencode in TUI as markdown content).

Desired change
- Add a small integration layer for the CLI: a function that accepts text and a flag or opts and returns rendered CLI-safe output using the existing renderer, with a size guard and TTY-aware behaviour.
- Wire the integration into a small set of commands initially (help text generation, `wl` error output, and any commands that emit code samples). Make the change opt-in behind a flag and/or config.
- Add unit tests and update docs describing the flag, supported Markdown subset, and safety considerations for CI logs.

Related work
- src/tui/markdown-renderer.ts — in-repo renderer implementation.
- src/tui/components/detail.ts, src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts — examples of renderer integration.
- tests/unit/markdown-renderer.test.ts — unit tests for renderer.
- WL-0MNC79G3P004NZXH — Markdown formatting in Description and Comments field (related, shows precedent of reuse).

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "May I ask follow-up questions during intake?" — Answer (seed instruction): "do not ask questions". Source: provided seed argument. Final: yes, respected (agent inference).

Notes

Risks
- Large or complex Markdown inputs in logs could slow commands; mitigate by size guard.
- Preservation of blessed tags might be incomplete; mitigate by adding targeted tests.
- This intake prefers reusing the existing renderer to limit dependencies. If the team prefers a different renderer for CLI constraints (e.g., smaller/no dependencies, different output control), update constraints and success criteria accordingly.

Related work (automated report)

# Intake Brief: Add TUI shortcut to create new work item

Headline summary

Add a keyboard shortcut and dialog to the TUI for creating new work items without leaving the interface.

## Problem statement

Users currently cannot create new work items directly from the TUI interface. They must exit the TUI and use the CLI `wl create` command, which disrupts workflow and reduces productivity.

## Users

- **Developers and project managers** who use the TUI as their primary interface for managing work items. Example user story: "As a TUI user, I can create a new work item without leaving the TUI so I can quickly capture new tasks without disrupting my workflow."

## Success criteria

- [ ] A keyboard shortcut opens a "Create Work Item" dialog in the TUI
- [ ] The dialog provides input fields for: title (text input), description (multiline textarea), issue-type (dropdown/list: bug, feature, task, epic, chore), priority (dropdown/list: critical, high, medium, low)
- [ ] Dialog has "Create Item" and "Cancel" buttons with standard TUI styling
- [ ] Pressing `Ctrl+S` in the dialog creates/saves the work item
- [ ] Pressing `Escape` or clicking "Cancel" closes the dialog without creating an item
- [ ] On successful creation, the dialog closes, a toast confirmation appears, and the new item appears in the TUI list
- [ ] The new item is persisted to the database via the existing `db.create()` API
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and TUI help menu

## Constraints

- Must follow existing TUI dialog patterns (similar to Update dialog in `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts`)
- Must use blessed.js widgets consistent with existing TUI components
- Keyboard shortcuts should not conflict with existing shortcuts (check `src/tui/constants.ts`)
- Creation must use the existing database API (`db.create()`) via `src/tui/persistence.ts` patterns

## Existing state

- The TUI has an update dialog (`updateDialog` in `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts`) that provides a pattern for multi-field dialogs with lists and textareas
- The controller (`src/tui/controller.ts`) handles dialog lifecycle, keyboard shortcuts, and database operations
- Keyboard shortcuts are defined in `src/tui/constants.ts` with the `DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS` array for help menu display
- The help menu component (`src/tui/components/help-menu.ts`) displays available shortcuts
- The database API supports `db.create()` for creating new work items

## Desired change

1. Add a new `createDialog` component to `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts` with:
   - Title input field (text input)
   - Description textarea (multiline)
   - Issue-type list (bug, feature, task, epic, chore)
   - Priority list (critical, high, medium, low)
   - "Create Item" and "Cancel" buttons
   - Focus management for field navigation (Tab/Shift+Tab)

2. Add keyboard shortcut handler in `src/tui/controller.ts` to open the create dialog

3. Implement form submission logic that:
   - Validates required fields (title)
   - Calls `db.create()` with the form data
   - Shows success/error toast
   - Refreshes the TUI list to show the new item

4. Update `src/tui/constants.ts` to add the new shortcut to `DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS`

5. Add Ctrl+S handler within the create dialog for quick submission

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: Additional fields (tags, assignee, stage) may be requested; record these as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item's scope
- **Keyboard conflict risk**: Need to verify shortcut doesn't conflict with existing shortcuts; may need to choose alternative
- **Assumption**: Title is the only required field; description, issue-type, and priority have sensible defaults (empty, 'task', 'medium')

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed intent provided sufficient detail to draft this intake brief. Implementation details were inferred from existing TUI patterns in the codebase:
- Dialog structure follows the existing `updateDialog` pattern in `src/tui/components/dialogs.ts`
- Keyboard shortcut handling follows patterns in `src/tui/controller.ts`
- Database operations follow patterns in `src/tui/persistence.ts`

The AMPA (Automated Multi-Project Assistant) system implements an automated intake process for work items. When the intake process identifies missing or insufficient information, it needs to:

# Intake Draft — Add --stage param to wl next (WL-0MNUOLCB20008HVX)

Headline: Add `--stage` filter to `wl next` to return recommendations constrained to a specific item stage.

Problem statement
-----------------
Add a `--stage` filter parameter to the `wl next` command so callers can request the next recommended work item constrained to a specific stage (for example `wl next --stage idea` should return the next most urgent item whose stage is `idea`).

Users
-----
- CLI users (developers, producers, agents) who use `wl next` to determine the next work item to work on.
- Automation and agents that script `wl next` and expect deterministic filtering.

Example user stories:
- As a developer, I want `wl next --stage idea` to surface only items in the `idea` stage so I can triage items in that stage.
- As an automation script, I want to restrict `wl next` recommendations to `in_progress` items for monitoring.

Success criteria
----------------
- `wl next --stage <stage>` returns the top candidate(s) matching the requested stage and preserves existing ranking logic.
- Human and JSON output formats are supported and behave consistently with existing `wl next` semantics.
- Passing test coverage added for at least three stages (idea, in_progress, done) including edge cases where no matching items exist.
- Documentation updated: CLI reference, tutorials that mention `wl next`, and examples.
- Full project test suite passes.
- Help text for `wl next` must list all legal stage options in the CLI help and examples.

Constraints
-----------
- The `--stage` parameter must be optional and must not change default behaviour when omitted.
- Accept a single value only (single-value filter).
- Stage values must be canonical exact strings used by the system (for example: `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_progress`, `in_review`, `done`). The CLI must validate input against that canonical set and reject unknown values with a clear error and non-zero exit code.
- Backward compatibility: `wl next` without `--stage` must behave exactly as before.
- Performance: filtering by stage must not add significant overhead to the selection algorithm.

Existing state
--------------
- `wl next` currently supports filters such as `--assignee`, `--search`, `--include-blocked`, and `--no-re-sort` (see CLI.md and src/commands/next implementation). There is no `--stage` filter today.
- The selection pipeline in `src/database.ts` includes a consolidated filter pipeline and explicitly removes in-progress items during candidate selection; tests reference expectations about skipping in-progress items.

Desired change
--------------
- Add `--stage <stage>` option to the `wl next` command parser and CLI docs.
- Wire the option into the candidate selection pipeline so only items with the matching canonical stage are considered.
- Implement strict validation against canonical stage strings; do not implement synonym normalization. Update CLI help to enumerate valid values.
- Add unit and integration tests and update documentation.

Related work
------------

# Intake Brief: TUI Freeze When Metadata Shows GitHub Hint

## Problem Statement

The TUI freezes or becomes unresponsive when selecting work items whose metadata pane displays the GitHub hint line "GitHub:   (set githubRepo in config to enable)" (3 spaces between colon and parenthesis). The freeze is caused by synchronous work performed during the metadata update flow, including expensive formatting operations (humanFormatWorkItem), markdown rendering (renderMarkdownToTags), and synchronous database I/O (db.getCommentsForWorkItem called in updateDetailForIndex).

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using the TUI to view and manage work items
- **User Story**: As a user, I want the TUI to remain responsive when navigating through work items, even when they display the GitHub configuration hint, so I can efficiently triage and update work items without UI stutters or freezes blocking my interactions.

## Success Criteria

1. **Reproduction Test**: With the provided repro steps (selecting an item without githubRepo configured), the TUI no longer becomes unresponsive while displaying the GitHub hint.
2. **Latency**: The metadata pane update path (controller.updateDetailForIndex → metadataPane.updateFromItem) completes in under 50ms for typical items on a dev machine.
3. **Tests**: Existing tests that assert the GitHub hint remain passing (UI semantics preserved).
4. **No Regressions**: No new blocking I/O introduced; core functionality of metadata rendering preserved.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not change persisted data formats or public APIs.
- Avoid heavy architectural rewrites in the first PR; prefer lightweight fixes and targeted caching or selective work avoidance.
- It is acceptable to move heavy formatting offline later, but first prioritize short-term, low-risk mitigations that can be reviewed quickly.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: During investigation, additional freeze causes or optimization opportunities may be identified. Mitigation: Record these as new work items linked to this item, do not expand current scope.
- **Instrumentation inconclusive**: Micro-timings may not clearly identify the culprit if the freeze is intermittent or environment-dependent. Mitigation: Use multiple test items and repeat measurements.
- **50ms threshold assumption**: The 50ms latency target is based on initial estimates; may need adjustment after baseline measurements.
- **Reproducibility assumption**: The freeze is assumed to be reproducible on current main branch; if not, investigation may require additional repro steps.
- **Detail cache interaction**: The existing detailCache caches `humanFormatWorkItem` for the detail pane but not metadata pane; fixes should consider whether metadata pane should use similar caching.

## Existing State

The TUI periodically freezes during metadata pane updates. The parent epic (WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T) addressed JSONL export freezing, but this specific issue with the GitHub hint metadata display persists. The relevant code paths are:

- `src/tui/components/metadata-pane.ts` — `MetadataPaneComponent.updateFromItem(...)` calls `humanFormatWorkItem`, `renderMarkdownToTags`, and constructs the GitHub hint
- `src/tui/controller.ts` — `updateDetailForIndex(...)` calls `metadataPane.updateFromItem` and potentially `db.getCommentsForWorkItem`
- `src/tui/markdown-renderer.ts` — `renderMarkdownToTags` implementation
- `src/lib/github-helper.ts` and `src/commands/github.ts` — GitHub config resolution helpers

Initial hypotheses for the freeze:
- `humanFormatWorkItem(item, ...)` used to derive audit excerpt is expensive and may traverse/format many fields synchronously
- `renderMarkdownToTags` invoked in setContent does markdown parsing + tag injection synchronously
- `db.getCommentsForWorkItem` may perform synchronous I/O or slow SQLite queries in the hot path
- The combination of any of the above during metadata update for every item selection causes the event loop to block

## Desired Change

Implement lightweight, short-term mitigations to reduce or eliminate the freeze:

1. **Instrumentation**: Add conditional micro-timing logs (enabled when --perf or verbose) around the metadata update path to identify the primary culprit.
2. **Cheap Audit Excerpt**: Replace `humanFormatWorkItem` call in metadata pane with a lightweight excerpt function when only a one-line audit excerpt is needed.
3. **Skip Markdown for Plain Lines**: Detect simple plain-text lines (like the GitHub hint) and bypass `renderMarkdownToTags` for them.
4. **Async Comment Count**: If `db.getCommentsForWorkItem` is slow, fetch comment count asynchronously and update metadata when available.

If instrumentation shows heavy formatting is unavoidable in the hot path, design a background worker or caching strategy in a follow-up item.

## Related Work

- **Epic: Fix TUI Freezing Issues** (WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T) — Parent epic, now completed. This item is a remaining freeze issue not addressed by the epic's changes.
- **Remove autoExport: SQLite as single source of truth with ephemeral JSONL** (WL-0MN53C1BZ17WJRBR) — Completed infrastructure change
- **Slow down investigation** (WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6) — Related investigation work
- **Async JSONL export / background refresh** (WL-0MNAZFYP10068XLV) — Related async work
- **Prototype incremental rendering** (WL-0MNAL79K20048STX) — Related rendering work
- **TUI doesn't update description and meta data (cache invalidation)** (WL-0MND0NYK2002F0BW) — Related cache issue
- **Links to metadata output** (WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU) — Related metadata work
- **Test file**: `tests/tui/tui-github-metadata.test.ts` — Shows GitHub hint test pattern

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "The parent epic (WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T) is marked as completed. Should this work item be a child of that epic or remain standalone?" — Answer (agent inference): The epic is completed, but this specific freeze symptom remains. The epic addressed the autoExport issue, and this item addresses a separate freeze trigger in the metadata pane. Given the epic is closed, this item should remain as a standalone bug fix linked by reference rather than as a child.
- Q: "Should acceptance criteria include a CI performance check or just local timing collection?" — Answer (from description): Start with local/perf-mode instrumentation; add a regression test later if stable.
- Q: "Is there any strong reason humanFormatWorkItem must be called for metadata pane?" — Answer (from description): Not definitively established; the suggestion is to try a lightweight path first and fall back to humanFormatWorkItem if needed.

Users

# Intake Draft: Always use audit skill for audit (WL-0MNVKUQKK002YIHX)

Problem statement
-----------------
When an audit is initiated (via CLI, TUI, or automated assistants) the command sent to opencode must explicitly invoke the audit skill so that audit-specific processing, formatting and traces are applied consistently.

Users
-----
- Developers and maintainers who run local audits or rely on audit output for triage and decision-making.
- Automated assistants (AMPA) and CI integration that invoke audits programmatically.

Example user stories
- As a developer, I want the audit invocation to use the audit skill so the resulting audit text and readiness semantics are produced consistently and rendered correctly in the TUI and CLI.

- All CLI/TUI commands and programmatic callers that create or update audits explicitly include the audit skill in the command sent to opencode (verifiable by code inspection and unit/integration tests).

**Constraints**
- Keep changes localized to TUI performance paths where possible.
- Avoid regressions in filtering, search, and selection behavior.

Problem statement:
Add a small, stable test-only API on TuiController (controller._test) that exposes dialog lifecycle and submission helpers so tests do not rely on private widget internals (like __opencode_* properties or blessed internals). This decouples tests from implementation details and reduces fragile test breakage during refactors.

Users:
- Primary: repository maintainers and test authors. Example user stories:
  - As a maintainer, I want tests to open/submit/close create and update dialogs using a stable API so refactors of widget internals do not break tests.
  - As a test author, I want a documented, minimal set of helpers on controller._test so I can write reliable integration tests without inspecting widget internals.

Success criteria:
- controller._test exists and is documented as a test-only/internal API.
- _test provides at minimum: openCreateDialog(), closeCreateDialog(), submitCreateDialog(), openUpdateDialog(), closeUpdateDialog(), submitUpdateDialog().
- Existing tests updated to use controller._test where they currently reach into __opencode_* properties or widget internals.
- No change to public runtime behavior or keyboard shortcut behavior.
- A short note added to tests/test-utils.ts or tests/tui/README describing the test API and example usage.

# Intake Draft — Re-sort on every DB update (WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW)

Problem statement
-----------------
Worklog currently provides a manual `wl re-sort` command and an automatic re-sort before `wl next` (WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF). The requested change is to run a re-sort after every database update (create/update) and once after batch operations (sync, gh *) so that sort_index is always current and high-priority items surface immediately without manual intervention.

Users
-----
- Operators and developers using the CLI/TUI who rely on `wl next` and list ordering to surface high-priority items.
- Release engineers and automation that programmatically create or update items and expect deterministic ordering.

Example user stories
- As an operator, when I create a high-priority item with `wl create`, I want it to appear above lower-priority items in subsequent `wl list`/`wl next` results without running `wl re-sort` manually.
- As a script that performs batch updates (wl sync or wl gh), I want ordering to be consistent after the batch completes.

Success criteria
----------------
1. Re-sort runs automatically after each non-batch CLI write (wl create, wl update) and once after batch operations (wl sync, wl gh *). The default behavior must match this rule. (measurable: integration tests that create/update items and assert expected ordering without invoking wl re-sort)
2. CLI flags to opt-out (--no-re-sort) and to force synchronous behavior (--re-sort-sync) are available and documented. (measurable: unit/CLI tests exercising flags)
3. Unit and integration tests cover the new behaviour, including performance-sensitive scenarios and preserving existing behaviour for completed/deleted items. (measurable: new tests added to tests/ and CI runs passing)
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (measurable: docs files updated and referenced in PR)
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (measurable: CI run / local test run passes)

Constraints
-----------
- Performance: Re-sorting can be O(n) and must not unacceptably degrade interactive CLI responsiveness on large databases. Default behaviour should prefer non-blocking/async execution for heavy operations.
- Idempotence: Repeated runs of the intake must not duplicate related-work entries or Appendix Q&A in the work item description.
- Scope: This intake focuses on wiring and flags; it should reuse existing reSort()/wl re-sort implementation in src/database.ts and src/commands/re-sort.ts rather than reimplementing sort logic.

Existing state
--------------
- `wl re-sort` exists (src/commands/re-sort.ts) and supports --recency, --dry-run, and gap options.
- A shared reSort() method and auto re-sort before `wl next` were implemented and merged (WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF). Tests and docs were added for that change.
- Migration and docs for sort_index exist (docs/migrations/sort_index.md).

Desired change
--------------
- Wire the existing reSort() API to run automatically after single-item write operations (wl create, wl update, wl comment add when it changes ordering-relevant fields, etc.).
- Ensure batch operations (wl sync, wl gh *) invoke a single re-sort after the batch completes (not per-item during the batch).
- Provide flags to opt out (--no-re-sort) and to force synchronous execution (--re-sort-sync). Default behavior for interactive commands should be non-blocking/async where possible.
- Add unit and integration tests to validate ordering, opt-out flags, and performance expectations.
- Update CLI.md and docs/migrations/sort_index.md to document the new automatic re-sort behaviour and flags.

Related work
------------
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF — Auto re-sort before wl next selection. Implementation completed: added reSort() in src/database.ts, auto re-sort in wl next, and flags --no-re-sort and --recency-policy. (Relevant: PR #774, PR #781)
- WL-0MKXTSWYP04LOMMT — Add sort_index column and DB migration. (Migration and docs completed)
- docs/migrations/sort_index.md — Migration guide and re-sort usage examples.
- src/commands/re-sort.ts — Current implementation of wl re-sort command and flags.
- WL-0MKZ4GAUQ1DFA6TC — Benchmark sort_index migration at scale (background perf guidance).
- WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T — Epic addressing TUI freezing; contains investigation and perf notes related to sorting at scale.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
---------------------------------------
- Q: "Do you intend WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW to request a behavior different from the completed WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF (which auto re-sorts before wl next and added a shared reSort() API)?" — Answer (user): "A" (Yes — auto re-sort after every CLI update/create/sync). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Evidence: WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF exists and implemented auto re-sort before wl next; this item expands scope to every DB update.

- Q: "If you want re-sort on every DB update, should the re-sort be: Synchronous immediate, Asynchronous/deferred, or Configurable per command?" — Answer (user): "c" (Configurable per command; default async but provide --sync or similar). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "Which acceptance criteria should be required?" — Answer (user): "1, 2, 3" (1: re-sort runs after non-batch and once after batch; 2: CLI flags; 3: tests). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- OPEN QUESTION: Exact list of commands that must trigger auto re-sort (e.g., should `wl comment add` trigger a re-sort if the comment changes nothing relevant?). Who to decide: Product/PM. Marked OPEN: Requires confirmation whether comments should trigger auto re-sort.

Related evidence & notes
- Implementation references: src/commands/re-sort.ts, src/database.ts (reSort implementation added by WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF), docs/migrations/sort_index.md.
- Tests: WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF added tests and passed (see PRs #774/#781). Use these tests as a template for new tests.

2. Parity tests are stable (flaky rate < 1% over 100 runs) and deterministic given fixed inputs.
3. Parity tests run within acceptable time bounds (each test or suite completes within reasonable timeout configured in CI).
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

- [ ] **Verify**: Toast confirms creation, dialog closes, new item appears in list

- [ ] **Verify fields present**: Status, Stage, Priority lists, Comment textarea
- [ ] **Change Priority**: Select different priority from dropdown
- [ ] **Submit**: Press Ctrl+S to save
- [ ] **Verify**: Toast confirms update, changes persisted, dialog closes

### Visual Inspection
- [ ] Modal borders: All dialogs have visible border lines
- [ ] Labels: Each dialog has a label (title bar) correctly displayed
- [ ] Positioning: Dialogs are centered on screen
- [ ] Styling: Border colors consistent (green for details, magenta for close, etc.)
- [ ] Responsive: Dialogs adapt to terminal resize

### Issues Discovered (see WL-0MO5XN3WK005CDS7)
1. Update dialog comment: Space key propagates to list (expands/collapses items)

These bugs prevent full verification of dialog functionality.
